brief: Kosovo's research layer on cash and payments rests on three legs: the BQK's own working-paper series (highest authority, bot-defended, and the usual place where new payment/inclusion indicators appear first), independent think tanks led by Riinvest and GAP (the only survey-based estimates of informality and undeclared income, which serve as the de-facto proxy for cash intensity), and a long tail of Albanian-language university theses — chiefly the openly harvestable UBT Knowledge Center and the Mitrovica thesis portal — that contain small original surveys on card and e-banking usage. English-language peer-reviewed work is thin but real, concentrated in a small cluster of Kosovo academics publishing cashless-adoption and internet-banking surveys, best tracked through RePEc and author pages rather than journal by journal. The clearest structural weakness is Serbian-language coverage: the north-Kosovo dinar-to-euro cash story is documented mainly by community NGOs and media rather than by indexed research, so it needs a dedicated sr-language discovery pass.
